maya_s: AcmeOps reported intermittent tool call failures when uploading images via the TS SDK — 'ocr_extract' returns schema validation errors.

jared_sdk: Can you paste the root request payload + the API error? short log is fine.

maya_s: Here's the sanitized payload they sent (captured in their Node app):
```json
{"tool":"ocr_extract","args":{"attachment":Buffer.from(file)}}
```
(their logger printed a Buffer object)

maya_s: API error returned:
```json
{"error":"ToolSchemaError","message":"Invalid type for field 'attachment': expected base64 string, got object"}
```

li_runtime: Likely cause: Node Buffer objects serialize to {"type":"Buffer","data":[...]} when JSON.stringified -> runtime sees an object not a string. Two knock-on issues: schema validation fails, and our tool-selector hashing uses JSON.stringify(args) so a different representation changes the selector hash.

jared_sdk: Repro we ran locally (very small):
```ts
const buf = fs.readFileSync('./img.jpg');
await client.tool.call('ocr_extract', {attachment: buf});
```
Result: API rejects with ToolSchemaError. If we do `attachment: buf.toString('base64')` it works.

ryan_devex: Go SDK marshals []byte -> base64 string by default, so Go callers didn't hit this. TS/Node leaving Buffer as-is explains 'sometimes works' (users who b64 manually) vs failing for ones that rely on automatic JSON serialization.

maya_s: Shared workaround with customer: set `attachment: Buffer.from(buf).toString('base64')` or use helper `client.utils.b64(buf)`. Also suggested adding header `x-client-schema: 2` if they can to enable tolerant decoding.

jared_sdk: Plan: open PR to (1) normalize Buffer/Uint8Array/ArrayBuffer -> base64 on request path, (2) adopt a stable/canonical stringify for tool-selector hashing so representations don't change selection, (3) add unit tests covering Node/browser/deno. ETA: tomorrow EOD.

ryan_devex: :thumbsup: Can we add a short-term runtime guard to accept `{type: 'Buffer', data: [...]}` and coerce to base64 to reduce customer impact?

li_runtime: Yes — will add tolerant deserializer and increment a metric `toolcall.buffer_object_received` so we can roll it back once adoption is high. Will canary that today.

maya_s: Customer informed and applying workaround. I'll follow up if they see regressions. Thanks everyone.

support_bot: Note: created ticket INF-4128 to track SDK fix + runtime mitigation.
